summary: A Buddhist studies scholar, Kyoshi Renja completed doctoral coursework (attested 2013) and held a research post (研究生) at Taisho University.

Kyosho Hayashima (1914–1999) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at Toyo University and Yokohama City University in 1962, and served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (attested 1980).
Kyosho Tanaka (b. 1947) studied Buddhist studies at the University of Tokyo (~1966–1975). He served as an associate professor at Musashino University from circa 1975 to 2017.
Kyoshun Todo (1916–2002) was a Buddhist studies scholar who served at Bukkyo University as an assistant professor (attested 1962) and later as a professor (attested 1988–1992).
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Kōdō Yotsuya earned an MA at Komazawa University and completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg.
A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Kōichi Furusaka studied under Hakuyu Hadano and served as a professor at Osaka Kyoiku University (attested 1991).
Laeticia Söderman is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology who earned an M.A. (completed 2010) and pursued graduate studies (attested 2014) at the University of Helsinki.

Lal Mani Joshi (1935–1984) studied at Allahabad, Gorakhpur, and Banaras Hindu University, completing his doctorate under Govind Chandra Pande (~1961–1964). He was a visiting professor at Haverford College (~1980–1981) in Buddhist, Indological, and religious studies.
Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi worked in Indology, holding positions as a Jain Pandit at Baroda Central Library and at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1939).

Lama Palden Drolma, active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied under traditional teachers including Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Jamgön Kongtrül the Third, Bokar Rinpoche, Situ Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, Druptop Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche, and Khenpo Tsültrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.
Lama Yeshe Gyamtso, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studied under traditional teachers Lama Norlha and Kalu Rinpoche (attested 1996).

Lambert Schmithausen (b. 1939), an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, earned his doctorate under Erich Frauwallner (1963) and studied under Paul Hacker. He held professorships at the University of Münster (~1970–1976) and the University of Hamburg (1973–2005).

Lance E. Nelson specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctorate at McMaster University (1986) and held a professorship at the University of San Diego (attested 1997).

Lance S. Cousins (1942–2015) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He held posts at Manchester (~1970–2000), Oxford (~2000–2015), and Wolfson College (~2002–2015), and was president of the Pali Text Society (~1994–2002).
Lang Chen, working in Buddhist studies and sinology, earned a PhD at Yale University (attested 2015) supervised by Koichi Shinohara and Phyllis Granoff, and also studied under Janet Gyatso.

Lang Eun Ra is a doctoral student in Buddhist studies and philosophy at Temple University, where Charles Wei-hsun Fu served as doctoral supervisor and Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert M. Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler were teachers.
Lara Braitstein, active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, completed a PhD at McGill University, where she studied under Richard P. Hayes.

Larry DeVries completed a PhD at the University of Minnesota and worked in Indology and religious studies. He taught at Minnesota, Hawaii, and Washington, held a research position at Chicago, and was affiliated with Langara College (attested 2005).

Lars Fogelin completed a PhD at the University of Michigan under Carla Sinopoli (1995–2003) in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held posts at Albion College, Southern Illinois University Carbondale, and the University of Arizona.
Lars Martin Fosse (b. 1950) specializes in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Heidelberg, Bonn, and the University of Oslo (~1975–1997), later teaching at Oslo (attested 2002).
